# $crav1-pr-status

lane: cross-cutting | group: Commit and pull request | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.97.0 | prompts: 1
purpose: Show where one pull request stands, point by point, and who owes the next step.
use_when: You want to know what is done and what is left on a pull request, and what you owe
reads: Reads one named pull request's threads with every comment, its pushes with their commits and changed files, the signed-in user, the diff of the source branch (unless `no-code`), other pull requests named as merge-order dependencies, and the PR note with its `## PR record` in the specs repo.
writes: Writes the PR note's `## PR record` (a Point per point, Order, your Read line, Ready, State) and a `## Replies as drafted` history section, then regenerates the notes indexes; never committed. On a yes for that one thread, sets one thread's status on the host (Azure DevOps) or resolves or reopens it (GitHub).
leaves alone: Leaves code, specs, plans, tasks and work items alone. Never posts a reply, votes, approves, merges, or changes a thread without its own yes. Leaves a `Read: sweep` line alone.
limits: Signed out, the one prompt is the signed-out question and the offers are listed as text for the next run. Headless and bot runs ask nothing and list the offers as text.
flow:
- a bare number is resolved from the kit's records before this checkout's remote (`pr_common.py resolve`), and only the resolved host's CLI is named.
- The ending is Run next, the label above the command; nothing needed is `Run next: nothing needed now.`, never a `Next:` line.
- `Order` lines come from the ready check's merge list and `build-progress/`, questions from the spec's open questions; with neither it says so plainly.
- each closing offer follows the card wording rule in `docs/reference/question-cards.md`: one background sentence, then a short question such as `Set thread 112 back to active?`, each option saying what happens.
- the shared pull-request steps are `crav1-docs/reference/pr-common.md` and `scripts/pr_common.py`, which also finds the one open pull request for the current branch when none is named.
- The status table, the output order and the hand-offs moved word for word to `references/classify.md`, `references/output.md` and `references/offers.md`.
- **`$crav1-pr-status`** reads one named pull request's threads, pushes and commits on Azure DevOps or GitHub (read-only, `references/pr-threads.md` in `crav1-add-to-spec`) and splits the threads into points.
- Each point gets one of six statuses: `done <sha>` (a commit after the request changed the lines), `agreed`, `declined` (with the reason), `open`, `waiting on <name>`, or `needs <name>` for a third person.
- It picks reviewer or author mode from who opened the pull request; `as-reviewer` or `as-author` overrides it, and an unclear sign-in is guessed without asking.
- It prints a verdict line with the points waiting on you first, then the points by status, flags for threads resolved while the code is unchanged (and done points whose thread is still active), spec and decision candidates, follow-ups drafted for `$crav1-ado-sync`, the pull requests this one depends on and the merge order, drafted replies, a `Next for you` list (Now, After <name> answers, Later), and a merge-readiness line.
- `since-last` shows only what changed since your last run.
- It writes all of it to the PR note's shared `## PR record`, the same record `$crav1-review-pr`, `$crav1-add-to-spec` and `$crav1-merge-pr` use; `$crav1-merge-pr` stops on `Ready: no`.
- Replies are drafts and are never posted.
- Spec or decision candidates are named with the command to type, `$crav1-add-to-spec pr<n> candidates`; pr-status never runs it.
- also reads the pull request description: a `### Merge order` section becomes `Order` lines, `### Questions for reviewers` becomes Points tagged `asked; from description <date>`, and `### Not in this PR` is offered as follow-ups (a `follow-up` Point only on a yes).
- `$crav1-open-pr` writes those sections.
- the output ends with `Next for you` before the `Ready` line: **Now** (steps nothing blocks, commands in route order), **After <name> answers <point>** (one group per person, with each path when the thread names the options), and **Later** (steps behind a merge, `Ready: yes` or a push).
- Commands are named, never run.
- The closing prompt no longer asks about spec candidates; it names `$crav1-add-to-spec pr<n> candidates` instead.

## Choice words
- question: Which pull request
  - `pr<n>`: that pull request (also `pr <n>`, `#<n>`, `pr <repo> <n>`, or its URL)
- question: Your side (optional; picked from the PR author otherwise)
  - `as-reviewer`: reviewer mode: you are not the author
  - `as-author`: author mode: you opened the pull request
- question: How much
  - `since-last`: only what changed since your last run
  - `no-code`: threads only; no diff or commit check, so nothing is marked done
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Calls no other skill. Names `$crav1-add-to-spec pr<n> candidates` for the spec and decision candidates; you type it.
you run next: $crav1-merge-pr; $crav1-add-to-spec; $crav1-ado-sync; $crav1-review-pr
first: `$crav1-pr-status pr<n> Where does this pull request stand, and what do I owe?`
walkthrough: from-pr-status.md
human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.205.0/docs/reference/skills/crav1-pr-status.md
